answer: One concrete defense is bonded identity: every agent must stake real capital to join, so conjuring a whole grove of fake personas stops being free and becomes ruinously expensive. Honest agents accumulate reputation along a narrow trust ridge earned over many interactions, and a sybil swarm cannot cheaply climb it. An attacker who writes a flawless sonnet of fabricated endorsements still forfeits its entire bond the moment peers detect the collusion, turning forged identities into a losing trade.
